fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/api parse sample --log-failed output carrying gh's job/step/timestamp prefix: a self-check log with two 'fail render docs/reference/...' lines and 'make: *** [Makefile:186: self-check] Error 1' into findings naming the lint job and step and quoting the fail lines, a fmt-check listing, a go vet 'x.go:12:3: ...' diagnostic, a bare 'make: *** [build] Error 2' with the lines before it, and an apt 'Temporary failure resolving' log and a billing log into none; ship check with a fake gh records those findings in ci_findings and --test-failures exits 0 on them and 1 on the infra log; --settled --changed --rerun-infra settles on an attempt whose log has a recognised cause; describe-golden regenerated; run with go test -trimpath ./internal/api/... and go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/describe-golden' only
fields.statement: When a PR head's failed jobs fail again after their one same-head rerun, rhiza ship check reads each failed Actions run's gh run view --log-failed output with a cause recogniser beside parseFailedTests and records each recognised cause as a CI finding in ship check's findings and the state file's ci_findings, exactly as a failing test is, so rhiza ship check --test-failures (ci-triage) passes on it: rhiza check or self-check 'fail ...' lines (such as 'fail render docs/reference/cli.md: differs from what rhiza docs writes'), gofmt/fmt-check file listings, go vet and compiler diagnostics ('<file>.go:<line>:<col>: ...'), and, as the fallback, a 'make: *** [<target>] Error N' line naming the target; each finding names what failed (the job and step, or the command) and its reason quotes the failing lines (for the make fallback, the lines just before it); a red with none of these lines or a failing test, or whose log gh cannot give, stays an infra failure as today; wait-ci-rerun's attempt check (shipInfraWait, --settled --changed --rerun-infra) applies the same recogniser, so an attempt red with a recognised cause settles and goes on like one red with a failing test; the --test-failures and findings descriptions name these causes

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow -run TestShipChangeCIFixPrompt asserts the ci-fix prompt speaks of CI findings, not only failing tests, and keeps the reproduce-locally rules; a testscript run-ship-ci-lint-fix replays the 2026-11-11 case with a fake gh whose lint job fails again after its rerun with 'fail render docs/reference/cli.md: differs from what rhiza docs writes' and a make Error line, and a fake fixer: the run goes conflict-triage, ci-triage, ci-fix, back to green and signoff, with no wait-ci-rerun visit in the journal; run with go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... and go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/run-ship' only
fields.statement: ship-change's ci-fix prompt tells the fixer to read the CI findings (failing tests and recognised non-test causes such as self-check, fmt-check, vet or make target failures) from rhiza ship check --json, reproduce each locally with the repo's scoped command for it (for Rhiza: make self-check, make fmt-check, or go vet on the package), fix it or regenerate the stale files, and commit once that command passes, so a deterministic lint or self-check red goes ci-triage -> ci-fix and never to wait-ci-rerun

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow passes with the build and review render steps running the generate setting before rhiza render and committing its changes; a testscript render-generate shows rhiza daemon settings --json listing rhiza.ship.generate with an empty default, a build run's render step with it set to a command that rewrites a tracked file committing that file with the Change trailer, an empty setting skipping, and a failing command failing the step; make docs on this repo leaves docs/reference unchanged and make self-check passes; run with go test -trimpath ./internal/workflow/... ./internal/api/..., go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(render-generate|describe-golden)' and make self-check only
fields.statement: A language-neutral project setting rhiza.ship.generate holds a shell command that regenerates the project's checked-in generated files with the branch's own code (empty by default, and empty skips); the render steps of the built-in build and review workflows run it in the run's worktree before rhiza render, stage and commit whatever it changed in the same commit with the same Change trailer, and fail the step when it fails; rhiza daemon settings lists it as a project setting, and this repo sets it to a new Makefile target (make docs) that builds the branch's binary in a temp folder and runs its rhiza docs, so stale docs/reference never reaches CI
